body.statement: Under effective \(K\)-valued inputs, \(\operatorname{Cert}_{uv,m,G}(B,Q)\) terminates and is sound and complete. It returns incompatibility exactly when \(\mathcal S(B,Q;G)=\varnothing\); conditional on \(\mathcal S(B,Q;G)\ne\varnothing\), it returns one rational function exactly when \(\mathcal H_{uv}(B,Q;G)\) consists of one rational function; otherwise it returns two attained stable pairs \((A,D),(A',D')\in\mathcal S(B,Q;G)\) satisfying \((A_{vu}-A'_{vu})^2+(A_{vu}A'_{vv}-A'_{vu}A_{vv})^2>0\). The certificate remains complete for zero diagonals, zero queried edges, open fibers, positive-dimensional fibers, and branch mergers.
body.justification: A total formula-or-ambiguity output replaces numerical root selection by an auditable causal identification certificate.
body.gap: Classical CAD decides semialgebraic formulas and classical root methods select branches; neither provides this target-aware graph-recursive contract with covariance filtering and exact transfer-distinct witnesses.
body.consumer: Software for subsampled process-DAG analysis can refuse false singleton answers and furnish two explicit observationally equivalent causal explanations when identification fails.
body.proof_tex:
Use one variable for every graph-allowed lower-triangular entry of \(A\) and one variable \(d_i\) for every diagonal entry of \(D\).  The compatible fiber is the realization of the following finite semialgebraic system over \(K\):
\[
 A^m-B=0,\qquad
 \sum_{r=0}^{m-1}A^rD(A^r)^\top-Q=0,\qquad
 -1<A_{ii}<1,\qquad d_i>0,
\]
together with the fixed graph-zero equations and \(D_{ij}=0\) for \(i\ne j\).  All matrix powers and covariance entries are polynomials in these finitely many variables.  Because \(A\) is triangular, the strict diagonal inequalities are equivalent to \(\rho(A)<1\), and because \(D\) is diagonal, the inequalities \(d_i>0\) are equivalent to \(D\succ0\).  Thus this semialgebraic realization is exactly \(\mathcal S(B,Q;G)\), with neither closure nor endpoint points added.

The diagonal equations are \(A_{ii}^m=B_{ii}\).  There is one real root when \(m\) is odd and zero, one, or two real roots when \(m\) is even, so the certificate has finitely many diagonal branches.  On a branch, Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}path\mbox{-}expansion}\) expresses each coordinate in increasing endpoint gap as
\[
 A_{ij}C_m(A_{ii},A_{jj})=B_{ij}-R_{ij,m}(A).
\]
Whenever the displayed coefficient is nonzero, exact division eliminates \(A_{ij}\); when it is zero, the coordinate and its polynomial equation remain in the residual system.  Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}divided\mbox{-}difference\mbox{-}zero\mbox{-}set}\) decides which case holds on each isolated diagonal branch.  Clearing only products of denominators already constrained to be nonzero preserves equivalence.  The certificate then retains every unused transition equation, every graph-zero equation, every covariance equation, and every strict stability and positivity inequality.  Consequently the finite union of its residual systems has realization exactly \(\mathcal S(B,Q;G)\).

Apply Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}effective\mbox{-}cad\mbox{-}decision\mbox{-}sampling}\) to these residual systems.  It terminates and reports all of them empty if and only if \(\mathcal S(B,Q;G)=\varnothing\).  This proves the incompatibility branch and its soundness and completeness.

Suppose now that the fiber is nonempty.  Write
\[
 p=A_{vu},\quad q=A_{vv},\qquad
 p'=A'_{vu},\quad q'=A'_{vv}.
\]
Stability ensures that \(1-qz\) and \(1-q'z\) are nonzero on \(\mathbb T\).  The two transfers are identical rational functions if and only if cross multiplication gives the polynomial identity
\[
 p(1-q'z)=p'(1-qz).
\]
Equality of the constant and linear coefficients is equivalent to
\[
 p=p',\qquad pq'=p'q.
\]
Therefore they are unequal exactly when
\[
 (p-p')^2+(pq'-p'q)^2>0.
\]
This test correctly treats the zero-edge case: all pairs \((0,q)\) give the same zero transfer even if their second coordinates differ.

Form a two-copy semialgebraic system by taking two copies of the complete compatible-fiber constraints and adjoining the last strict inequality.  The CAD sampling lemma decides its feasibility.  If feasible, its exact sample consists of two attained points of the original strict fiber and hence gives the two stable transfer-distinct witnesses asserted in the theorem.  If infeasible, every two compatible points have equal transfers.  A sample from the nonempty one-copy system then supplies their common rational function; if its numerator is zero the output is canonically the zero function.  Thus the singleton-transfer and ambiguity outputs are both sound and complete.

No step replaces a strict inequality by a weak one or assumes a zero-dimensional realization.  Hence zero diagonal roots, open and positive-dimensional fibers, and branch mergers remain covered.  As exact destructive checks, take \(d=2,m=3,B=0,Q=I_2\).  The two interior points
\[
 A_{\pm}=\begin{pmatrix}0&0\\ \pm1/2&0\end{pmatrix},
 \qquad D_{\pm}=\operatorname{diag}(1,3/4)
\]
both satisfy the complete fiber constraints and have transfers \(\pm z/2\), so the two-copy system is feasible and the certificate cannot return a singleton or an endpoint-only artifact.  For \(d=2,m=2\), any compatible point with \(A_{21}\ne0\) has a second compatible point \((-A,D)\): evenness gives \((-A)^m=A^m\), and each covariance summand is unchanged because
\[
 (-A)^rD((-A)^r)^\top=A^rD(A^r)^\top.
\]
The ambiguity inequality has first term \((2A_{21})^2>0\), so the certificate necessarily retains this global sign pair.
